name: Drinking water treatment; source water acquisition infrastructure; at plant
description:
This unit process reflects infrastructure components associated with the  source water acquisition drinking water treatment process. The process is normalized to the functional unit of 1 cubic meter of treated drinking water. 

Key information is available in process metadata. Full process documentation is available in EPA report number 600/R-14/376
category: 22: Utilities/2213: Water, Sewage and Other Systems

processDocumentation.geographyDescription: The case-study facility is located in Cincinnati Ohio and this process reflects the topography and scale of that facility. Background datasets have been selected to represent U.S. average conditions. This unit process may not be useful as background data in other contexts.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: Includes infrastructure associated with 2 intakes, 2 pump stations, and piping from Ohio River at GCWW Richard Miller Treatment Plant.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: Inventory exchange values were sourced directly from the cited EPA report on disinfection options in municipal drinking water treatment. Background data sources have, in some cases, been updated to reflect newer and/or public data sources. Elementary flows were mapped to the federal elementary flow list.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: Infrastructure components, excluding piping, include only material and installation inputs and exclude flows associated with manufacturing of mechanical components such as pumps and tanks. Infrastructure end-of-life treatment/disposal is excluded. The mass balance for this process was not calculated.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: Primary data was provided by representatives of the Greater Cincinnati Water Works Richard Miller Treatment Plant.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Infrastructure was standardized to the functional unit by dividing the inventory value by the quantity of water treated over the lifespan of the infrastructure component. Inventory data was developed based on the drinking water treatment system in Cincinnati Ohio, which treats an average water volume of 123,560,247 cubic meters per year.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: This drinking water unit process is part of a larger product system that models the full scope of flows necessary to estimate environmental impacts of drinking water delivered to the consumer. The scope of the model includes water acquisition, treatment, distribution and infrastructure processes. End-of-life disposal of infrastructure materials is excluded from the model scope. Primary data was provided by representatives of the Greater Cincinnati Water Works Richard Miller Treatment Plant. Uncertainty ranges are not available for this data.
processDocumentation.useAdvice: This process represents infrastructure requirements at Cincinnati's Richard Miller Water Treatment facility and reflects the size, technology and geographic characteristics of their system. This unit process may not be useful as background data in other contexts.

sources.name: Xue et al (2019) LCA of Urban Water Systems

reviews.details:
Proof reading details: Passed
Other details: none

processDocumentation.intendedApplication:
This is an infrastructure process used in the development of drinking water LCI data, which is intended to be used as a background process by LCA practitioners, industry and the general public.  The specificity of this process may limit it's usefulness as background data in other projects. 

Situation C2 - Accounting, without system-external interatctions. The intended application is a purely descriptive accounting / documentation of the analysed system excluding existing interactions with other systems in the LCI model.
processDocumentation.projectDescription: Data were prepared by Eastern Research Group (ERG) on behalf of the U.S. EPA under Contract No. EP-C-12-021, "Environmental and Cost Life Cycle Assessment of Disinfection Options for Municipal Drinking Water Treatment"
